name: Lion President
summary: R123's Lion President: a bubbly Aussie V8 sedan in the spirit of the last V8 Commodore, the SS-V Redline. Gloss-black roof, two big forward-facing bonnet nostrils, angular lamps with LED fangs, a wide lower grille split by one thick bar, slatted air curtains, side skirts, a tall wing on posts, a full-width tail lamp on a black band, a black diffuser with quad exhausts, red calipers and a black-and-gold shoulder pinstripe. Code-built from a generated reference sheet (R81). Rear drive, 1700 kg: the Hawk Dash's spec twin.
feedback: Comment on this page (what to change, which view or state); the session turns each comment into a bug bead that cites this page and the car's id.

specTwin.sharedSpec: One spec, two bodies (R123): the Hawk Dash and the Lion President name spec 'aussie-v8' in web/shared/src/roster.json, and their profiles' handling (tuning) is identical, held by tools/vehicles/test/spec-twins.test.mjs. Rear drive, 1700 kg, Cruz-like launch, more power per kilo for a higher top speed; the bodies (hull, wheels, damage parts) are each car's own.

reference.note: The reference sheets were generated with Muse Image from a written brief (art/vehicles/lion-president/refs/prompts/), the Cruz Missile's sheet given as the layout example. Per view: the reference crop, the model shaded, and the silhouette diff (green is model only, red is reference only). Scored by tools/vehicles/fit (Spike J's method: perspective camera, the same mask pipeline on both sides, the contact-shadow band left out).

damage.note: Left to right: intact; door_FL and door_RL loose; front and back loose; wheel_FL cambered; front detached; door_FL detached; back detached; wheel_FL detached; both front doors and the back detached; a stripped shell. Posed in a three.js viewer about each part's hinge line (tools/vehicles/evidence).

paints.pattern: Seat colour on the paint key (white texels tint; the black roof, pinstripe, glass, lamps and tyres keep their colour), the number on the black roof (anchor roof_number) and in the HUD badge. paints-strip.png shows white plus five player colours. Known defect br-vhtm: filtered livery edges are untinted grey.

findings.text: contract + reproducibility (validator clean, origin between the axles, anchors cam_fp, cam_tp_target, com, roof_number, lplate_front, lplate_rear; no badges, logos or real names)

budget; WARN silhouette: weighted IoU 0.935 for LOD0 against 'lod + 1' (side 0.949, top 0.922, front 0.921, rear 0.938) and 0.941 for LOD2 against 'lowest', short of the ~0.95 target. The reference's lower front is boxier and wider than the shared lofted body allows, and the wing is kept high for identity

by-eye cues: black roof, bonnet nostrils, fang lamps, split lower grille, tall wing, full-width tail lamp, quad exhausts and the shoulder pinstripe read in views.png and grid-1.png; at grid-24 it reads apart from the Hawk Dash (wing, black roof, tail band against twin stripes)
paint key / one material (the Cruz's atlas layout and material; draws per tile are the Cruz's 11 parts, one InstancedMesh per part type)
damage states (each part turns about its hinge line to its limit; detached parts lie as separate bodies; dark bays and interior blocks behind missing panels)
physics fit (convex collider per part from the bake, colliders.png; profile geometry synced from the sidecar; rear drive, 1700 kg, the Hawk Dash's tuning exactly)
identity at the smallest tile: legible in grid-24.png; the pinstripe reads light (cream) through the paint key's filtered edges (br-vhtm, renderer-wide). The roof number isn't drawn by this viewer.
detail: the calipers read as small red squares on the rim disc; LOD2's flat scoop decals are partly clipped by the faceted bonnet
